newsitem.title: USA: Helms-Burton disrupting world trade - Axworthy.
newsitem.headline: Helms-Burton disrupting world trade - Axworthy.

text.p: Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Tuesday the controversial U.S. anti-Cuba sanctions law called Helms-Burton is causing a "real disruption" in the larger world trading system.

After talks with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, he said the U.S. refusal to cooperate with a World Trading Organization effort to adjudicate the sanctions dispute "confirms my own anxiety that Helms-Burtom is causing a real disruption in the larger trading system."
"It does set a real turbulence as we're seeing over the dispute on WTO applications," said Axworthy.

"That's something we've all worked almost a decade to bring about, which is an effective world trading system with a set of rules, which is going to be thrown off track by Helms-Burton," Axworthy told reporters outside the State Department.

Canada and Europe have been outraged by Helms-Burton, which among other things, allows naturalized Americans to sue in U.S. courts foreigners deemed to have benefited from property confiscated by the Cuban government since the communist revolution in 1959.

The European Union took the dispute to the WTO. But last month, Washington challenged the fitness of the WTO to adjudicate the dispute and said it would not cooperate with the WTO investigative panel in this case.
